defects.summary: `artefacts-and-locked` is a NOTE at exit 0 and tells the reader the hook will clean the artefacts up at the next session start. The real hook does the opposite: `may_replace` refuses the directory, the skill is NOT installed that run, and the session-start verdict goes DEGRADED. So round 3 replaced a true-but-mis-explained red with a false green that hides the exact verdict skills-doctor exists to explain.
defects.evidence: Measured by driving the REAL hook (.claude/hooks/skills-bootstrap.sh) twice against a file:// fixture registry, using scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py's own make_registry/make_project/_run_hook. Run 1 installs `alpha` clean. I then plant `alpha/__pycache__/h.cpython-311.pyc` - exactly what running a skill's own suite in place leaves - and confirm the doctor's reading (digest_skill_dir != recorded, digest_shared_payload == recorded, i.e. ARTEFACTS_ONLY). Run 2 output: `skills: 0/1 from file://...@4cb3b62 - DEGRADED: 1 shadowed - refusing to overwrite a directory this hook did not install, or that was edited since (alpha)`, and `alpha/__pycache__/h.cpython-311.pyc` is still on disk. Reading the code confirms why: may_replace (line 1013) compares the WHOLE-directory digest `have` against the locked digest and then against the recorded digest; with an artefact present it equals neither, so the function returns false, line 1077 does `shadowed+=("$name"); continue`, and no rm/cp runs. purge_locked_destinations only runs on bail-out paths (682/806/827/862/907/1155), never here. Three printed sentences are therefore false, and a reader can falsify all three by running the hook: (a) the note - "The hook digests the whole directory, so it still sees a mismatch: the directory is replaced at the next session start and those go with it"; (b) the note's justification - "No instruction byte is at risk, which is why this is a note rather than the edited-and-locked finding" - the byte-level risk is nil but the skill stops receiving updates for as long as the artefact exists, which is a decision for a human, the file's own definition of a FINDING; (c) SKILL.md line ~392 - "The hook still replaces the directory - its digest is the whole of it". The note's example list is also unmeasured: with only node_modules/ planted it still prints "the only difference is files the upload filter drops - a __pycache__, a .pytest_cache, a .pyc", none of which are present. `git log -S"replaced at the next session start"` -> bb7056e, this round. At 5b08678 the same shape was `[edited-and-locked]` at exit 1; the fix moved the verdict the wrong way rather than correcting the sentence. Supporting: the sibling artefacts-and-stale case is also exit 0 while the hook says `DEGRADED: 1 skill no longer in the lock left in place`.

defects.summary: PRE-EXISTING: `edited-and-locked` and `hand-placed-over-locked` both promise the directory is destroyed at the next session start. The hook refuses to touch either one - it reports DEGRADED/shadowed and leaves the bytes alone. These are the two sentences bb7056e's new note was written to mirror, so the round-3 text inherited a claim that was already wrong.
defects.evidence: Both measured by driving the real hook. EDITED: install alpha, append "MY LOCAL EDIT" to alpha/SKILL.md, re-run -> `skills: 0/1 ... DEGRADED: 1 shadowed - refusing to overwrite a directory this hook did not install, or that was edited since (alpha)`, and the edit survives. The doctor prints "The directory does not survive the next session start, so any local change here is lost without a prompt." HAND-PLACED: install alpha, replace it with a hand copy and empty the record, re-run -> same DEGRADED/shadowed verdict, hand copy survives. The doctor prints "it will not survive the next session start, which replaces the directory with the registry's copy, or removes it outright if the project ships a skill of the same name. Move it if you want to keep it." The hook's own comment at may_replace (line 1007) states the rule the doctor contradicts: "installed but EDITED since (the user has taken ownership of it) ... is somebody else's." `git log -S` puts both sentences at b0a23c1, so the verdict (exit 1) is right and only the remedy text is wrong - but "move it if you want to keep it" tells a user to act on a loss that will not happen, and both texts should say what the hook actually does: refuse the skill, hold it at 0/N, and go DEGRADED.

defects.summary: A cell the matrix omits: no cell exercises `shadow-copies-differ`. `matrix_store` always plants a byte-identical account copy, so the shadow observation has only one outcome in the whole cross-product - and the fix report's own stillOpen list of never-emitted kinds omits this one while naming four others.
defects.evidence: matrix_store's shadow arm is `account_copy(store, TARGET, body=BODY, crlf=False)`, byte-for-byte the personal copy, so all six reachable shadow cells expect `{shadowed-by-the-account-store}` and none can produce the divergent kind. The uncovered kind is precisely the one at the centre of the round-2 defect the matrix was built to prevent recurring - a reader who takes the matrix for kind-complete would believe the divergent path is enumerated. It is not unasserted (14 references in the suite, including the depth-parametrised mutation test at line 3127), so nothing is untested; the defect is that the matrix's completeness test proves pair-completeness while the surrounding comment claims cell-completeness, and the stillOpen disclosure that would have flagged it is itself incomplete. Cheapest fix: make the account copy's content a fifth axis value rather than a fixture constant.
